record.paper_title: Neutrino-nucleus interactions: open questions and future projects
record.context_brief: Neutrino probes of poorly known nuclear excited states
record.original_question: What experimental information can be obtained about the nuclear excited states probed by neutrinos in the charged-current 208Pb(νe, e−)208B reaction, especially states with multipolarities Jπ = 0−, 1−, and 2− for which little information is available and higher-multipolarity states for which no information is available?

evidence.quote: In particular, neutrinos can be used to perform nuclear structure studies since neutrinos probe nuclear excited states for which little or no experimental information is available (Figure 1) [22].
Note that little experimental information is available on the Jπ=0−, 1−, 2− states and none on those having higher multipolarity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the charged-current neutrino reaction on lead, 208Pb(ν_e, e^-)208Bi, in which an incoming electron neutrino converts a neutron in the 208Pb target into a proton, producing an outgoing electron together with the residual nucleus 208Bi (here written 208B by abuse of notation). The cross section receives contributions from excitations of 208Bi having various spin-parity quantum numbers J^π, with the relative weight of each multipolarity depending on the incoming neutrino energy.

For 208Bi nuclear excited states with multipolarities J^π = 0^-, 1^-, and 2^-, present experimental information on excitation energies, transition strengths, and branching ratios is sparse, and for states of higher multipolarity (e.g. J^π = 3^-, 4^-, 5^-, ...) essentially no direct experimental data are available, even though such forbidden transitions of high multipolarity provide the dominant contribution to the cross section at supernova-relevant neutrino energies.

Problem. Devise experimental strategies (using neutrino beams, charge-exchange hadronic reactions such as (p,n) or (3He,t), photonuclear or electron-scattering probes, β-decay measurements, or supernova-neutrino detectors employing lead as a target) capable of providing quantitative information on the energies, widths, and transition strengths of the J^π = 0^-, 1^-, 2^- excited states of 208Bi populated by the charged-current reaction 208Pb(ν_e, e^-)208Bi, and on excited states of higher multipolarity J^π ≥ 3^- for which no experimental information currently exists. Determine what combination of such measurements is sufficient to constrain the multipole decomposition of the 208Pb(ν_e, e^-)208Bi cross section at neutrino energies relevant to stellar core-collapse (E_ν ≲ 80 MeV).
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that calculations of the 208Pb(ν_e,e^-)208Bi cross section (e.g., via charge-exchange RPA) rely heavily on theoretical models because direct experimental data on 208Bi excited states with J^π = 0^-, 1^-, 2^- are limited and data on higher-multipolarity states are essentially absent. The HALO supernova-neutrino detector at SNOLAB uses lead as a target, but no published measurement to date provides multipole-resolved experimental constraints on these states. Charge-exchange (3He,t) and (p,n) experiments have constrained Gamow-Teller and spin-dipole strengths in 208Bi, but the requested broader experimental program remains an open task.

status_evidence.title: Charged-current neutrino-208Pb reactions
status_evidence.snippet: Forbidden transitions of high multipolarity represent the main contribution in reactions of neutrinos on nuclei as heavy as lead.
status_evidence.claim: Cross section is dominated by high-multipolarity transitions, motivating need for experimental input on those states.

status_evidence.title: Gamow-Teller and spin-dipole strength in 208Bi and neutrino-induced reactions
status_evidence.snippet: Gamow-Teller and spin-dipole strength in 208Bi from charge-exchange experiments, used as input to neutrino-induced reaction predictions.
status_evidence.claim: Only low-multipolarity (GT, spin-dipole) strengths have been measured; higher multipolarities remain experimentally unconstrained.

status_evidence.title: Experimental neutrino physics in a nuclear landscape
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews experimental neutrino-nucleus measurements and outstanding nuclear-structure uncertainties.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2024) review still lists nuclear-structure inputs to ν-Pb cross sections as poorly constrained.
